AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Adherence is paramount to the successful outcome of exercise-based treatment.

AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE OF STUDY
AbstractText.content: The barriers and enablers to adherence to a home- and class-based exercise program were explored in this qualitative study.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Semi-structured interviews were carried out to establish common themes relating to the participants' experiences during a year-long randomized controlled trial.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS/DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: Twelve participants were interviewed. The main enablers to exercise were highlighted as equipment, perceived benefit from the exercises, and longer and more intensive monitoring. Barriers included the lack of motivation, lack of equipment, and pain.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Implications for practice are incorporating enablers and addressing barriers including self-discharge from classes; the importance of longer term follow-up and the benefits of adopting exercise into a well-established routine may provide potential benefits.
